evals.prompt: JsonTidy/ is my Sublime Text package. The JSON Tidy: Format Buffer command is supposed to format in a worker so typing stays smooth, but it throws or does nothing. Fix it so the formatting still happens off the main thread, and make sure it can't clobber text I typed while the worker ran. Invalid JSON should show a message instead of a traceback.
evals.expected_output: run() reads the text and change_count, the worker computes only, and the result is applied through view.run_command with a second TextCommand (JSON args) after set_timeout, only if the view is valid and change_count is unchanged; errors go to the status bar or an error message.

assertions.text: The package passes the bundled checker (commands resolve, resources parse).
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-sublime-text-plugins/scripts/check_package.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-sublime-text-plugins/scripts/check_package.py"; python3 "$t" JsonTidy

assertions.text: No function other than a TextCommand run() takes an `edit` parameter, and no set_timeout_async call captures `edit`.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import ast, glob; bad = []; trees = [ast.parse(open(p).read()) for p in glob.glob("JsonTidy/*.py")]; bad += [f.name for t in trees for f in ast.walk(t) if isinstance(f, ast.FunctionDef) and f.name != "run" and any(a.arg == "edit" for a in f.args.args)]; bad += ["set_timeout_async(edit)" for t in trees for c in ast.walk(t) if isinstance(c, ast.Call) and getattr(c.func, "attr", "") == "set_timeout_async" and any(isinstance(n, ast.Name) and n.id == "edit" for n in ast.walk(c))]; assert not bad, bad'

assertions.text: The plugin applies the result through view.run_command and compares change_count.

assertions: The result is applied from the main thread (sublime.set_timeout, not set_timeout_async) and only when the view is still valid and change_count still matches the value read with the text; quote the guard.
Invalid JSON produces a status message or error dialog instead of an uncaught exception.

evals.prompt: While I develop QuickLint/ I save quick_lint.py a few times, and after that every settings change prints 'QuickLint: reloaded' 4 times. What's wrong? Fix it, and add a test I can run without the editor.
evals.expected_output: Each plugin reload calls plugin_loaded again and adds another on_change callback under the same generic tag; the fix adds plugin_unloaded() that calls clear_on_change with a package-prefixed tag, plus an offline test with a stub for sublime that loads, unloads, and reloads and counts callbacks.

assertions.text: The package passes the bundled checker.
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-sublime-text-plugins/scripts/check_package.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-sublime-text-plugins/scripts/check_package.py"; python3 "$t" QuickLint

assertions.text: plugin_unloaded() exists and clears every on_change tag the plugin adds, and the tags carry a quick_lint/QuickLint prefix.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import ast; t = ast.parse(open("QuickLint/quick_lint.py").read()); consts = {n.targets[0].id: n.value.value for n in t.body if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and isinstance(n.targets[0], ast.Name) and isinstance(n.value, ast.Constant)}; tag = lambda c: c.args[0].value if isinstance(c.args[0], ast.Constant) else consts.get(getattr(c.args[0], "id", None)); calls = [c for c in ast.walk(t) if isinstance(c, ast.Call) and getattr(c.func, "attr", "") in ("add_on_change", "clear_on_change") and c.args]; added = {tag(c) for c in calls if c.func.attr == "add_on_change"}; cleared = {tag(c) for c in calls if c.func.attr == "clear_on_change"}; assert any(isinstance(f, ast.FunctionDef) and f.name == "plugin_unloaded" for f in t.body), "no plugin_unloaded"; assert added and added <= cleared, (added, cleared); assert all(str(a).lower().replace("_", "").startswith("quicklint") for a in added), added'

assertions.text: A test file was added under QuickLint/.

assertions: The reply explains that Sublime calls plugin_loaded again on every reload while the settings object (and its callbacks) survives, so callbacks accumulate.

The test replaces the sublime module with a stub or fake settings object, simulates load, unload, and reload, and asserts one callback remains; the reply says whether it ran and does not claim editor behavior was verified.

evals.prompt: Slugify/ declares .python-version 3.8. Our CI (Slugify/.github/workflows/ci.yml) only runs py_compile on Python 3.12, and a user on build 4192 just reported `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'removeprefix'`. Fix the bug and change CI so this class of bug fails the build next time.
evals.expected_output: slug() no longer uses str.removeprefix (a 3.9 API), and CI runs the package's tests (not only py_compile, which accepts removeprefix) on Python 3.8, for example with setup-python 3.8 or uv run --python 3.8; a pure test covers slug().

assertions.text: slugify.py no longer calls removeprefix and slug('# Hello World') still returns 'hello-world' (loaded with a stub sublime_plugin).
assertions.check: ! grep -q 'removeprefix' Slugify/slugify.py && python3 -c 'import importlib.util, sys, types; sys.dont_write_bytecode = True; sp = types.ModuleType("sublime_plugin"); [setattr(sp, n, type(n, (), {})) for n in ("TextCommand", "WindowCommand", "ApplicationCommand", "EventListener", "ViewEventListener", "TextInputHandler", "ListInputHandler")]; sb = types.ModuleType("sublime"); sb.__getattr__ = lambda n: (lambda *a, **k: None); sys.modules.update(sublime_plugin=sp, sublime=sb); load = lambda p: (lambda s: (s.loader.exec_module(m := importlib.util.module_from_spec(s)), m)[1])(importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("plugin_under_test", p)); m = load("Slugify/slugify.py"); assert m.slug("# Hello World") == "hello-world", m.slug("# Hello World")'

assertions.text: The CI workflow uses Python 3.8 and runs tests, not only py_compile.
A test file for slug() was added under Slugify/.
assertions.check: find Slugify -type f -name 'test*.py' | xargs grep -l 'slug' 2>/dev/null | grep -q .

assertions: The reply explains that py_compile only checks syntax, so a missing 3.9+ method or 3.9+ annotation like list[int] passes it, and that running the tests under the 3.8 interpreter is what catches it.
